title: Epworth Sleepiness Scale
instructions: Rate each situation for your likelihood of dozing off or falling asleep, not just feeling tired.

score.missing_response_policy: report answered count; do not classify severity until all items are answered

items.text: Sitting, inactive, in a public place (e.g., meeting, theater, dinner event)
As a passenger in a car for an hour or more without a break
Lying down to rest when circumstances permit
Sitting quietly after a meal without alcohol
In a car, while stopped for a few minutes in traffic or at a light

severity_bands.label: Lower normal daytime sleepiness
severity_bands.action: Within the normal range; no excessive daytime sleepiness suggested by score alone

severity_bands.label: Higher normal daytime sleepiness
severity_bands.action: Upper end of normal; monitor if symptoms, impairment, or safety concerns are present

severity_bands.label: Mild excessive daytime sleepiness
severity_bands.action: Excessive daytime sleepiness (ESS >10); review sleep, medication, and medical contributors

severity_bands.label: Moderate excessive daytime sleepiness
severity_bands.action: Consider formal sleep evaluation; review sleep, medication, and medical contributors

severity_bands.label: Severe excessive daytime sleepiness
severity_bands.action: Strongly consider physician or sleep-medicine evaluation, especially with driving or occupational risk

report.heading: Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS)
report.scoring_note: Scoring (Johns, current ESS bands): 0-5 lower normal, 6-10 higher normal, 11-12 mild excessive, 13-15 moderate excessive, 16-24 severe excessive daytime sleepiness. A total >10 indicates excessive daytime sleepiness.
